messages.author: 7f0257cd1389289f
messages.subject: Re: Where should test data live when inst/tests -> tests/testthat
parts:
On 10 Mar 2014, at 17:37, Hadley Wickham wrote:

> Put it in tests/testthat?

The problem comes when you want to use testdata in examples. If you use an expression like

system.file('tests/testthat/testdata/nrrd/LHMask.nrrd',package='nat')

in an example then this will fail in check() – I guess precisely because the testdata might not be there if a user decides not to install the tests. The workaround we have so far is to wrap all examples that use testdata in \dontrun{} which seems a shame.

I guess the alternative would be to put some of the test data in e.g.

inst/exampledata

and restrict examples to that. But it is a bit unsatisfactory to have 2 sets of example/test data different places. Furthermore this fails

system.file('exampledata/nrrd/LHMask.nrrd',package='nat')

when using devtools::run_examples() but works with check() whereas the opposite is true for

system.file('inst/exampledata/nrrd/LHMask.nrrd',package='nat')

Any suggestions for improved arrangements very welcome.

Many thanks,

Greg.

PS Subject line now erm cleaned up. I assume it was an errant spellchecker rather than some subliminal reflection on this conversion process.

> On 11 Mar 2014, at 21:14, Hadley Wickham wrote:

>> are run with the correct working directory.
>
> That's right. The tests work fine in this setup. It's the examples (that I would like to use the same data) that are broken
>
> In an example:
>
> "testdata/nrrd/LHMask.nrrd" is broken with check() _and_ run_examples()
>
> if one puts the data in e.g. inst/exampledata
>
> "exampledata/nrrd/LHMask.nrrd" is broken with run_examples()
>
> "inst/exampledata/nrrd/LHMask.nrrd" is broken with check()

If you're using the data in examples, then it should go in inst/extdata.

You should be able to access that with `system.file("extdata", "nrrd",
"LHMask.nrrd', package = 'nat'). The problem is that that won't work
when developing your package, but devtools does some magic to make
work inside functions in your package. So write a function like:

exdata <- function(...) {
system.file("extdata", ..., package = 'nat')
}

That should work regardless of where you call it from.

Hadley
